book_table.title: books a table
book_table.cap: Three restaurants with room: you pick one, it asks before booking in your name.
book_table.alt: Screen recording of the app. You write “Book a table for Friday night”. The Daily agent opens a booking site showing three Italian restaurants with free tables and asks which one to book. Da Vinci at 8 pm is chosen. A card asks for your OK to send the booking in your name, and it is given. The agent answers that Da Vinci is booked for Friday, for 2, and added to your calendar.

sleep_week.title: sums up your week of sleep
sleep_week.cap: It reads your sleep data, draws the chart and suggests one thing to try tonight.
sleep_week.alt: Screen recording of the app. You ask “How did I sleep this week?”. The Coach agent reads your last 7 nights of sleep and shows a chart of the week. It answers: 7 h 12 on average, 25 minutes more than last week; on the nights you go to bed after midnight you lose over an hour of sleep; tonight, screens off at 10:30 pm?

subscriptions.title: cancels the subscriptions you forgot
subscriptions.cap: It finds two you no longer open, you choose, and nothing is sent without your OK.
subscriptions.alt: Screen recording of the app. You write “Cancel the subscriptions I don’t use”. The Budget agent finds CinePlus (€13.99 a month, not opened since July) and FitApp Premium (€9.99 a month, last workout in June) and asks which ones to cancel; both are chosen. A card asks for your OK to send the cancellation in your name, and it is given. The agent confirms both cancellations: up to €288 saved a year.

dinner.title: finds tonight’s dinner
dinner.cap: With what’s left in the fridge: a 20-minute recipe, and what’s missing for the list.
dinner.alt: Screen recording of the app. You ask “What’s for dinner tonight?”. The Home agent checks what’s left from Tuesday’s shopping, looks up a quick recipe and suggests courgette, feta and lemon pasta for 4, in 20 minutes, with its three steps. Only basil and parmesan are missing: it offers to add them to the shopping list.

weekend_lisbon.title: plans a weekend with friends
weekend_lisbon.cap: Shared with three friends: they vote on its cards from their link, for the date, then the flat, and each gets a task.
weekend_lisbon.alt: Screen recording of the app. An agent shared with three friends, Léa, Sam and Inès. You write “Lisbon with Léa, Sam and Inès: get us voting”. The agent posts a vote card, “Which weekend?”; the friends’ votes come in and the weekend of 21 November wins. It looks for flats and posts a second vote: Alfama, terrace, €92 a night, or Bairro Alto, rooftop, €105 a night, and the votes come in. Alfama wins and the agent shows the weekend list, a task for each of them.

private.where1: In your own space, separate from everyone else’s, on a server in the European Union (OVHcloud or Hetzner). Or on your own computer, if you install it at home.
private.where2: With All included, your space is backed up, encrypted, a few minutes after each activity, and at least once a day. The copy kept on our backup server can’t be read without the key, which stays in your space and on your devices.
private.who2: The AI reads what your agent sends it, to answer you: through EUrouter, a European AI router, then the provider running the model you chose. Before your first message, the app names the router and the model.
private.who3: Our limit, said plainly: as with any rented server, the host and we could technically get in. Our software doesn’t, and we only would if the law required it.

1.a: Your own AI agents, the Bips, in the app on iPhone, iPad and Android. They work in your own space, on a server in Europe that we look after: nothing to install, nothing to set up, updates and backups included.

2.a: Yes: a free week to start, if you never had one. We tell you before you pay when it ends and the price that follows. Stop before it ends and nothing is charged.

3.a: Each plan has its AI credit for the month: about 7,000 messages for Solo, 13,000 for Duo, 24,000 for Family with the default model, shared by everyone in it. The app shows it as an estimated number of messages with your model: a simple exchange counts as one, a task in the browser for much more (often several dozen). In Duo and Family, the person who pays sees how much each person uses, never what they write, and can set a limit per person. What’s left carries over to the next month. Need more: extra credit in the app, and it never expires. Month’s credit used: your conversations go on; routines and the browser resume next month or as soon as you add credit.

4.a: Not us: Kerfy Studio doesn’t read them or train any AI on them. To answer you, the AI reads what your agent sends it: through EUrouter, a European AI router, then the provider running the chosen model; the app names the router and the model before your first message. As we rent the server, we could technically enter your space: our software doesn’t, and we only would if the law required it. Your relatives only read what you share with them: one of your agents, read-only, and the family agent’s shared conversation.

5.q: How do Duo and Family work?
5.a: Each invited person has their own account, space and agents; the plan’s AI credit is shared. Paying gives access to no one’s conversations: the person who pays only sees how much credit each person uses. With Family, up to six people share the same plan and its credit.

6.q: Can I stop whenever I want?
6.a: Yes, at no cost: the subscription ends at the end of the paid period. Your space is then kept for 30 days so you can take everything with you, then erased with its backups. And you have 14 days to change your mind after buying.

7.q: Why is it cheaper on the web?
7.a: In the app, the App Store and Google Play take a commission. On the web it’s smaller, so we pass it on to you. Same service: you sign in to the app with the same account.

8.a: Both, and iPad too: iOS 18 or later, Android 10 or later. In English, French, German and Spanish.

9.a: Nous Research’s open-source AI agent. BipAgents is an independent app built on it: it turns your Hermes agents into Bips you take everywhere.

10.a: The app is free: one command installs it on your computer or server, and you only pay for the AI model you pick. The subscription spares you all that.

11.q: Which AI model, and is it any good?
11.a: With the subscription, GLM-5.3 Flash, the same for everyone, picked by Kerfy Studio. For everyday tasks (email, calendar, searches, bookings), it comes very close to the top models. Before your first message, the app names the router and the model’s maker. On your own computer, you bring the model of your choice.
